audit.feedback: editorial_review_rejected: Card1 (info): shows palm grove over excavated mud-brick foundations — matches Diriyah ruins description, fine. Card3: identical Diriyah excavation/palm-grove photo, consistent and relevant to the mud-brick building claim. Card2 'تراث عالمي': the image actually shows a framed photograph/print of an old mud building mounted on a wooden wall indoors (looks like a museum or shop display), not the real At-Turaif district itself — a photo-of-a-photo misrepresenting the UNESCO site, so relevant=false. Card4 'من التاريخ للسرعة': the image is an open-wheel Formula E race car on a generic street circuit with grandstands; its credit (Gobierno CDMX, 2017) indicates this is from the Mexico City ePrix, not Diriyah's track — it does not actually depict the Diriyah race described in the text, so relevant=false. Because two of four images do not truthfully depict their claimed subject, visual_identity fails overall even though the textual claims themselves trace correctly to the source (c1–c3, c5, c6).

unknown_visual_selection: Diriyah ePrix race car: البطاقات الثلاث الأولى عن موقع الدرعية التاريخي أطلال وحفريات، فاستخدمنا صور الدرعية المتاحة (إعادة الإعمار وموقع الحفر) لأنها تمثل المكان نفسه بشكل عام دون افتراض حدث محدد. أما بطاقة سباق الفورمولا إي فلا توجد صورة مناسبة في الكتالوج؛ لافتة ADR الألمانية غير ذات صلة إطلاقاً بموضوع السباق أو الدرعية، فتم استبعادها ووضع null.

unknown_visual_selection: UNESCO heritage certificate: Card 1: chose a generic modern Arabic coffee dallah photo (162286835) since it shows the traditional pot itself without claiming a specific event, matching the described object. Card 2: the 1737 map of Mocha port (68793953) directly illustrates the historic Yemeni port mentioned as coffee's origin point. Card 3: no image shows cardamom-spiced coffee specifically; the closest neutral option is a generic 'Arabic coffee and chocolate' serving photo (57709080), used to represent the coffee-serving ritual rather than a specific location. Card 4: none of the supplied UNESCO certificate images relate to Arabic coffee's heritage listing—they show unrelated crafts from Austria, China, and Armenia—so no suitable image exists and null is returned.

editorial_review_rejected: Card1: shows ornate silver/brass dallah pots with steam rising, matches text about dalla brewing and finjan cups - fine. Card2: old French 1737 port plan/map of Mocha, Yemen with ships - correctly illustrates c5 about Mocha's origin, appropriate historical map. Card3: historical painting of Mecca with Kaaba at center surrounded by hills and buildings - correctly illustrates c6 about coffee spreading to Mecca/Hejaz. Card4: photo shows dark brown coffee with thick pale foam/crema in a white cup WITH a handle - this visually resembles Turkish-style coffee or regular brewed coffee, not traditional Arabic qahwa which is typically pale golden/light amber colored and served in a small handleless finjan poured from a dallah (as correctly shown in card1). Using this foamy dark-roast-looking coffee to represent 'القهوة العربية' and its UNESCO-recognized hospitality ritual is a lookalike mismatch that could mislead viewers on what authentic Saudi/Arabic qahwa looks like, so this card is rejected for relevance despite readable text.
